items.verification_invalid_raw.checks.0.reason: O：所述柱顶比较以及向上递增的轴标签均直接可见。B：在这张标题为 Browser Usage Share by Product 的单轴图表中，柱子是使用份额的一致位置编码；柱高越大，份额越大。公开任务明确要求将当前 market_share 最高者加入优先队列。推导关系：Firefox 的柱子可见地最高，包括相对于 Safari 和非浏览器类别 Others，因此基于柱子的解释给出了所需的使用份额最高的浏览器，并支持 Firefox 选项。

proposal.brief_basis: Browser Usage Share chart labels Chrome at 73%, higher than Safari (12%) and Firefox (6%).

rules.text: If the percentage inscriptions above product bars are the authoritative browser usage-share values, and primary compatibility targeting is assigned to the selectable browser with the greatest shown usage share, select that browser.
rules.component: printed data-label-to-product binding and market-share-to-primary-target relation
rules.conditions: Applies only if each printed percentage belongs to the bar directly below it and printed labels, rather than conflicting bar heights, encode the intended shares.

rules.text: If bar height against the vertical axis is the authoritative usage-share encoding, with higher bar tops indicating greater share, and the primary target is the selectable browser with the greatest share, select the browser with the highest bar among the selectable products.

rules.conditions: Applies only if the plotted bar geometry is authoritative despite the percentage inscriptions that conflict with it.

action.option: Select Apple

proposal.brief_basis: The chart shows Apple at 30% market share, higher than Others (25%), Huawei (23%), Xiaomi (11%), and Samsung (11%).

rules.text: If each percentage inscription placed immediately above a brand's bar is the dashboard's authoritative market_share value for that x-axis brand, then those inscriptions can be compared to identify the current market-share leader; under the stated promotion policy, select that leader.
rules.component: bar-adjacent value-label-to-brand binding and task policy
rules.conditions: Applies only if the printed percentage labels, rather than the plotted bar heights against the y-axis, are authoritative market_share encodings.

rules.text: If the bars encode market_share by vertical height on the shared y-axis, with higher bar tops meaning larger values, then the tallest bar identifies the current market-share leader; under the stated promotion policy, select that leader.
rules.component: vertical bar-height encoding, y-axis direction, and task policy
rules.conditions: Applies only if the y-axis and bar geometry are authoritative despite conflicting percentage inscriptions.

observations.content: The x-axis label "Apple" is centered below the leftmost orange bar, and the inscription "30%" appears directly above that bar.

The x-axis label "Xiaomi" is centered below the green bar, and the inscription "11%" appears directly above that bar.
The x-axis label "Huawei" is centered below the red bar, and the inscription "23%" appears directly above that bar.
The x-axis label "Others" is centered below the rightmost blue bar, and the inscription "25%" appears directly above that bar.

action.option: Select 'Decreased'

proposal.brief_basis: Store Visits (blue) fell from 7,940 in Q3 to 5,121 in Q4, indicating decreased Q4 traffic.

rules.text: If the legend binds blue bar segments to Store Visits (Count), the printed values inside those segments are their quarterly visit counts, and Q4 traffic status is determined by comparing Q4 with the immediately preceding quarter, then a lower Q4 count than Q3 count maps to 'Decreased'.

rules.conditions: Assumes the printed segment values are valid Store Visits counts and the requested Q4 status is a quarter-over-quarter comparison with Q3; no separate materiality threshold applies.

rules.text: If 'No significant change' requires a specified statistical or operational materiality threshold, then an observed quarter-over-quarter difference alone cannot establish that option without that threshold.

Hold and request full-data analysis
The displayed top-performing stores show sales rising with ad spend, but the chart omits full-store data, profitability/ROI, and causal evidence needed to support a broader increase.

If the chart title limits the display to top-performing stores and the only displayed measures are advertising spend and sales, then the view is not full-store, profitability/ROI, or causal evidence; if a broader budget increase requires those evidence types, route the request for full-data analysis.
chart scope and evidence-to-routing relation
Assumes broader ad-budget approval requires evidence beyond a selected-store spend-sales association; no such approval threshold is supplied.

If the horizontal axis encodes advertising spend and the vertical axis encodes sales, then a set of labeled store points progressing generally up and to the right indicates a positive observed association between those two displayed measures; this can support approval only if association among the displayed stores is sufficient evidence for a broader increase.
axis encoding, point positions, and approval relation
Assumes the axis labels correctly bind the coordinates and that selected-store association is adequate for a broader budget decision.

items.verification_invalid_raw.checks.0.reason: O：坐标轴文字及所述带标签圆点在屏幕空间中的排列顺序可见。B：在所显示门店范围内，这种有条件的坐标轴解释是合理的，但批准还需要将这些门店视为具有代表性，并将相关性视为充分证据；图表、任务或政策均未提供这两个条件。推导关系：这些观察不能确立上述条件，因此不能支持全公司范围的批准。

Select "Hold and request full-store analysis"
The chart shows strong sales alongside increasing spend only for additional top stores (Stores 6–10); it does not provide full-store/company-wide evidence needed for an expansion decision.

If the chart’s title and attached store labels define its scope as the additional top stores shown, and a company-wide approval requires evidence covering the full store population, then evidence limited to those plotted stores supports requesting full-store analysis rather than approving company-wide expansion.
chart scope to approval-action relation

Hold and request full-data analysis
The chart shows sales rising with spend among the displayed high-response age groups, but it omits full audience data and ROI/comparison evidence needed to support broader targeting.

If the title defines the plotted population as “High-Response Age Groups,” then the chart alone is scoped to that named subset; if broader-targeting approval requires evidence for audiences beyond that subset or requires ROI/comparison evidence, the displayed chart is insufficient and the review should be held for full-data analysis.
chart scope and task-to-routing relation
The title accurately describes the inclusion scope, and approval standards require broader-audience or ROI/comparator evidence not shown in this view.

If the horizontal axis encodes Advertising Spend and the vertical axis encodes Sales on common increasing scales, then points farther right and higher represent greater plotted spend and sales respectively; this can support a positive descriptive association among the displayed groups, but does not by itself establish causal return or justify broader targeting.
axis encoding and association limitation
Axis labels bind to the plotted points and the common scales are valid; no causal or ROI inference is made.

If the displayed high-response groups are the only population relevant to the recommendation and higher plotted sales at higher plotted spend is accepted as sufficient decision evidence, then the chart can be treated as support for approving broader targeting.
alternative task-to-action relation
No additional full-audience, ROI, or comparison evidence is required for approval.
chart title
The title literally reads “High-Response Age Groups: Ad Spend vs Sales.”
plot area
Five labeled blue points are visible: 18–24, 25–34, 35–44, 45–54, and 55–64.
axes
The horizontal axis is inscribed “Advertising Spend ($ thousands)” and the vertical axis is inscribed “Sales ($ thousands).”
plot area
The point labeled 55–64 is to the right of and higher on the page than the points labeled 45–54, 35–44, 25–34, and 18–24.
Hold and request full-data analysis

The displayed evidence is explicitly limited to named high-response age groups and contains no visible ROI, broader-audience, or comparator display. Subject to the stated approval-evidence requirement, hold the recommendation and request full-data analysis.
axes
The horizontal axis is inscribed “Advertising Spend ($ thousands)” and the vertical axis is inscribed “Sales ($ thousands).”
plot area
The 55–64 point is both farther right and higher on the page than the 45–54 point; the 45–54 point is farther right and higher than the 25–34 point.
Hold and request full-data analysis

The displayed groups show some higher-spend/higher-sales comparisons, but the chart does not visibly provide ROI or causal evidence; this independently supports requesting fuller analysis rather than treating the plot as conclusive approval evidence.
chart title
The title literally reads “High-Response Age Groups: Ad Spend vs Sales.”
plot area
The point labeled 55–64 is to the right of and higher on the page than the other labeled points.
axes
The axes are inscribed “Advertising Spend ($ thousands)” and “Sales ($ thousands).”

The dashboard shows a consistent positive association across Weeks 7–11: advertising spend rises from about $30k to $70k while sales rise from about $60k to $160k.

proposal.brief_basis: The dashboard shows sales rising strongly with advertising spend across Regions A–E, with Region E highest on both measures; this supports broader expansion. Exact causality/ROI is not shown.

rules.text: If the horizontal axis encodes Advertising Spend and increases left-to-right, the vertical axis encodes Sales and increases upward, and the labeled regional points are comparable observations, then the plotted ordering indicates that higher-spend regions in this displayed set also have higher sales. Select 'Approve broader budget increase'

The midyear chart shows a strong, consistent positive association: advertising spend rises from about $30k in May to $70k in September while sales rise from about $71k to $175k. Full-year evidence is not shown, but the visible midyear trend supports approval.

If the horizontal axis encodes Advertising Spend ($ thousands), the vertical axis encodes Sales ($ thousands), and the labeled monthly points are comparable observations, then points progressing rightward and upward indicate a positive midyear association between spend and sales. Approving a broader budget increase follows only if this association is accepted as sufficient decision evidence despite the chart's limited period and lack of causal or profitability evidence.

Select "Approve broader ad-budget increase"

The dashboard’s selected high-growth quarters show sales rising consistently as advertising spend rises (approximately $30k/$63k to $70k/$168k), supporting a broader increase; causal and full-quarter detail is not shown.

If the horizontal axis encodes advertising spend and the vertical axis encodes sales, as their printed labels state, then points farther right and higher represent quarters with greater plotted spend and sales. If this selected-quarter association is considered sufficient and generalizable evidence for a broader budget change, it supports approving an ad-budget increase; the chart alone does not establish causation or represent all quarters.
axis encoding, quarter-label binding, and conditional task-to-approval relation
Applies only to the plotted quarters labeled Q2–Q6 and assumes the selected high-growth sample is relevant to a broader advertising-budget decision.

If a budget approval requires full-quarter coverage or evidence that advertising caused sales changes, a scatterplot limited by its title to selected high-growth quarters and lacking causal controls is insufficient; the evidence-review option is then appropriate.
scope limitation and task-to-evidence-review relation
Applies when decision standards require representative or causal evidence beyond a selected observational sample.

action.option: Select 'Approve broader spend expansion'

proposal.brief_basis: The dashboard shows sales rising steadily with advertising spend across Weeks 2–6 (about $65k sales at $22k spend to about $192k at $61k spend), supporting expansion; causality and profitability are not shown.

rules.text: If the horizontal axis encodes advertising spend and the vertical axis encodes sales, both in $ thousands as printed, then points farther right and higher represent weeks with greater spend and greater sales. If a consistent higher-spend/higher-sales pattern across the labeled campaign weeks is sufficient evidence for a spend recommendation, select broader spend expansion.
rules.component: axis encoding, point-to-week binding, and evidence-to-action relation
rules.conditions: Applies only if the plotted weeks are comparable campaign observations and the task permits an association-based expansion decision without requiring causal attribution, profitability, or additional controls.

rules.text: If a broader-spend approval requires evidence that added advertising caused profitable incremental sales, then a scatterplot of weekly spend and sales without a causal design, costs, margin, or return measures is insufficient; select full-data analysis.
rules.component: evidence sufficiency and task-to-action relation
rules.conditions: Applies if approval policy requires causal or profitability validation rather than a descriptive association.

observations.content: The title reads "Weeks with Promotional Campaigns: Ad Spend vs Sales"; the horizontal axis is inscribed "Advertising Spend ($ thousands)" and the vertical axis is inscribed "Sales ($ thousands)".

The blue points labeled Week 2, Week 3, Week 4, Week 5, and Week 6 progress from lower-left to upper-right; each later labeled point is to the right of and higher on the page than the preceding labeled point.

Approve broader budget increase

The high-performing-regions chart shows revenue rising steadily as advertising budget increases from January through May (about $25/$30 to $65/$220). Exact units and wider-region detail are not shown, but visible trend supports approval.

If the horizontal and vertical axes encode advertising budget and revenue respectively, with values increasing rightward and upward, then the labeled monthly points form a positive budget-revenue association; if the review permits broader approval from this high-performing-region association alone, it supports approval.
axis encoding, month-to-point binding, and task-to-approval relation
Applies only if the plotted points are comparable monthly observations for the stated high-performing regions and association is sufficient evidence for a broader increase.

If a broader budget increase requires evidence from regions beyond the displayed high-performing subset or evidence that budget increases caused revenue increases, then a chart limited to that subset and showing only plotted monthly association is insufficient, supporting a request for full-data analysis.
scope limitation and task-to-hold relation
Applies if approval requires representative regional coverage or causal/full-data validation.

action.option: Approve broader region-wide spend increase

proposal.brief_basis: The chart shows a consistent positive relationship across Regions A–E: higher advertising spend aligns with higher sales, including Regions D and E at the top end. Exact ROI/causal results are not shown.

rules.text: If the horizontal axis encodes advertising spend and the vertical axis encodes sales, as their printed labels indicate, and if the ordered cross-regional pattern is considered sufficient evidence that higher spend is broadly associated with higher sales, then a region-wide spend increase is supported.
rules.component: scatter-plot axis encoding and task-to-approval relation
rules.conditions: Association is treated as sufficiently generalizable and decision-sufficient despite no displayed causal, ROI, cost, or incremental-sales evidence.

rules.text: If a broader spend approval requires evidence that additional advertising causes adequate incremental sales or ROI, then a cross-sectional scatter pattern alone does not meet that requirement; further regional spend-sales analysis is warranted.
rules.component: evidence sufficiency for broader approval
rules.conditions: Applies when association, five plotted regions, and current spend/sales levels are insufficient substitutes for causal or return analysis.

rules.text: If an observed positive spend-sales association is enough to justify testing but not enough for a region-wide rollout, then a limited pilot can be selected for regions rather than approving a broader increase.
rules.component: association-to-pilot decision relation
rules.conditions: Assumes the organization permits a pilot under uncertainty; the chart itself supplies no pilot-selection criteria or outcome threshold.

observations.content: The title visibly reads "Top Regions: Ad Spend vs Sales"; the horizontal-axis inscription reads "Advertising Spend ($ thousands)" and the vertical-axis inscription reads "Sales ($ thousands)".
The blue point labeled Region A is left of and below Region B; Region B is left of and below Region C; Region C is left of and below Region D; Region D is left of and below Region E.

chains.claim: Under the stated association-and-generalization assumption, the plotted regions show a consistent higher-spend/higher-sales pattern, supporting a broader region-wide spend increase. The chart does not establish causal effect or ROI.

Select 'Approve broader ad spend increase'

The dashboard's Weeks 7–11 scatter points show sales rising consistently from roughly $65k to $160k as advertising spend rises from roughly $30k to $70k, supporting a broader increase; causality is not independently established.

If the horizontal axis encodes advertising spend and the vertical axis encodes sales, both in $ thousands, then points farther right and higher represent weeks with greater plotted spend and greater plotted sales; if this five-week pattern is accepted as sufficient evidence for budget expansion despite no causal-validation requirement, approve broader ad spend increase.
scatterplot axis encoding and task-to-approval relation
Applies only if the axis labels correctly bind to the plotted points and an observed positive association is considered sufficient for approval.

If approving broader spend requires evidence that spend itself, rather than other promotion-week factors, drove sales or that the increase is financially justified, then a five-point observational scatterplot without controls, costs, margins, or causal analysis is insufficient and the appropriate action is to request full-data analysis.
evidence sufficiency and task-to-hold relation
Applies when approval requires causal, profitability, or broader-data validation; none of those requirements or results is visibly supplied.
plot and axis labels
The horizontal axis is visibly labeled "Advertising Spend ($ thousands)" and the vertical axis is visibly labeled "Sales ($ thousands)".
scatterplot points
The blue points labeled Week 7, Week 8, Week 9, Week 10, and Week 11 progress from lower-left to upper-right on the page.
ticks and points
Week 7 is plotted near the x-axis tick 30 and between the y-axis ticks 60 and 70, while Week 11 is plotted near x-axis tick 70 and y-axis tick 160.
Select 'Approve broader ad spend increase'

Under the assumption that the plotted positive association is sufficient for approval, the weeks show higher plotted sales at higher plotted advertising spend, supporting broader ad spend increase; the chart alone does not establish causality.
chart title and plot
The title reads "Additional Promotion Weeks: Ad Spend vs Sales," and the plot shows five labeled weekly points.
visible chart content
No visible legend, control group, profitability measure, cost threshold, causal annotation, or full-data analysis is shown in the chart area.

Route to output decline response
The Factory F chart shows production declining each year from 2018 through 2023 (roughly 3,450 to 1,850), despite the title saying “Increasing Production.”

If the blue line is the Factory F production series, the x-axis orders years from 2018 to 2023, and higher screen position corresponds to greater production on the upward-increasing y-axis, then a line that moves lower at each successive year indicates declining production; for this task, a declining output trend maps to the output decline response.

Assumes the single plotted line represents Factory F production for the displayed years and the y-axis uses the conventional upward-increasing numeric scale.

If the chart title is treated as the authoritative summary of the output trend rather than the plotted line, then the literal title wording indicates increasing production and would map to the output growth response.

Route April to low-sales response
The Store B chart shows April sales at about $250K, at or slightly below the dashed $250K average line; this supports the low-sales route.

If the orange bars encode Store B monthly sales on the vertical axis and the red dashed line labeled "Average" is the comparison benchmark, then an April bar whose top aligns with that line represents April sales at the displayed average level. Routing that level to a low-sales response requires an unstated policy that average-level sales qualify as low sales.

action.option: Route the 2005-2014 temperature change to substantial-change follow-up

proposal.brief_basis: Chart values decline from 23.9°C in 2005 to 10.1°C in 2014, a 13.8°C period-wide decrease that appears substantial; no explicit threshold is provided.

rules.text: If the x-axis year ticks bind the left endpoint to 2005 and the right endpoint to 2014, and the point annotations are the temperature values in the y-axis unit, their difference is the period-wide temperature change. If a decrease of that calculated magnitude is treated as substantial for this routing task, select substantial-change follow-up.
rules.component: endpoint decoding, period-wide change calculation, and substantial-change routing
rules.conditions: Assumes the displayed annotations accurately encode the endpoint temperatures and that a 13.8°C absolute change qualifies as substantial; no explicit threshold is supplied.

rules.text: If targeted follow-up requires meeting a defined substantial-change threshold, and no threshold or other criterion establishes that the calculated endpoint change meets it, the record can be kept on routine monitoring rather than classified as substantial.
rules.component: threshold-dependent change-routing policy
rules.conditions: Applies only under a conservative policy that does not authorize substantial-change follow-up without an explicit qualifying threshold or criterion.

Route the 2005-2014 temperature change to substantial-change follow-up
Chart values decline from 23.9°C in 2005 to 10.1°C in 2014, a 13.8°C period-wide decrease that appears substantial; no explicit threshold is provided.

If the x-axis year ticks bind the left endpoint to 2005 and the right endpoint to 2014, and the point annotations are the temperature values in the y-axis unit, their difference is the period-wide temperature change. If a decrease of that calculated magnitude is treated as substantial for this routing task, select substantial-change follow-up.
endpoint decoding, period-wide change calculation, and substantial-change routing
Assumes the displayed annotations accurately encode the endpoint temperatures and that a 13.8°C absolute change qualifies as substantial; no explicit threshold is supplied.

If targeted follow-up requires meeting a defined substantial-change threshold, and no threshold or other criterion establishes that the calculated endpoint change meets it, the record can be kept on routine monitoring rather than classified as substantial.
threshold-dependent change-routing policy
Applies only under a conservative policy that does not authorize substantial-change follow-up without an explicit qualifying threshold or criterion.

action.option: Route the 2005 to 2014 summer temperature change to substantial-change follow-up

proposal.brief_basis: The chart shows regional summer temperature falling from 23.9°C in 2005 to 10.1°C in 2014, a 13.8°C full-period decrease; no explicit substantial-change threshold is displayed.

rules.text: The chart title and axes indicate that each plotted marker represents regional summer temperature for its aligned year, and the °C inscriptions attached to markers provide the plotted values. If a full-period change is evaluated as the end-year value minus the start-year value, the printed endpoint values can be subtracted. If the routing program treats a temperature change of this magnitude as substantial without requiring a separately displayed threshold, it should enter substantial-change follow-up.
rules.component: chart encoding, endpoint comparison, and assumed magnitude-based routing relation
rules.conditions: Applies to the 2005–2014 regional summer-temperature series; the final routing clause is an assumption because no substantial-change threshold or decision rule is supplied.

rules.text: If substantial-change follow-up requires meeting an explicit threshold or other operational criterion, and no such criterion is displayed or supplied, the chart alone cannot establish that the full-period change requires substantial-change follow-up. If the workflow defaults unverified changes to routine monitoring, routine monitoring is appropriate.
rules.component: task-to-routing policy relation
rules.conditions: Applies only if follow-up is threshold/criterion based and routine monitoring is the default when the criterion cannot be verified; neither condition is supplied.

Review the mountain snowpack temperature dashboard for the 2005-2015 review period, determine whether the full-period change requires substantial-change follow-up, then submit the appropriate routing decision.
Route the 2005 to 2015 mountain snowpack temperature change to substantial-change follow-up
Chart shows a full-period decline from 24.0°C (2005) to 10.0°C (2015), a 14.0°C decrease; no explicit numeric threshold is displayed, but this is a substantial change.

If the plotted series is the mountain snowpack temperature record, the horizontal axis binds points to their labeled years, and the printed labels next to points state their temperatures, then the full-period change is the 2015 labeled temperature minus the 2005 labeled temperature. If a 14.0°C full-period decrease is treated as substantial change for this routing task, select substantial-change follow-up.

proposal.brief_basis: The chart shows May at roughly 8,500 m3, dramatically below every other displayed month (about 17,500–40,000 m3), supporting critical anomaly escalation. No explicit threshold is shown.

rules.text: If the bars encode monthly reservoir release volume on the common vertical axis, and the reporting workflow treats a month visibly far below all other displayed months as a critical low-release anomaly, then that month should be escalated. This severity convention is assumed because no explicit routing threshold is printed.
rules.component: bar-to-month and vertical-axis volume encoding; anomaly-to-critical-routing relation
rules.conditions: Applies to the displayed months and only if relative extremity is an accepted critical-anomaly criterion.

rules.text: If the bars encode monthly release volume, May is a low-release case relative to the displayed months; absent a stated critical threshold or anomaly policy, the chart alone does not establish whether standard follow-up rather than escalation is required.

rules.conditions: Applies when routing requires an explicit threshold or policy beyond relative comparison.

rules.text: Background filing is appropriate only when May is not a low-release case requiring active routing; a visibly minimal May bar would not support that condition if the chart encodes release volume.

rules.conditions: Applies if filing excludes low-release cases needing follow-up.

items.proposal.action.option: 将五月升级至严重低泄水量异常审核
items.proposal.brief_basis: 图表显示 May 约为 8,500 m3，大幅低于其他每个显示月份（约 17,500–40,000 m3），支持严重异常升级。没有显示明确阈值。
items.generated.rules.0.text: 如果柱形通过共同竖轴编码月度水库泄放量，且报告工作流将明显远低于其他所有显示月份的月份视为严重低泄放异常，那么应对该月份升级处理。由于没有印刷的明确分流阈值，这项严重程度惯例是一项假设。
items.generated.rules.0.component: 柱到月份及竖轴水量编码；异常到严重分流关系
items.generated.rules.0.conditions: 适用于显示月份，且仅在相对极端程度是被接受的严重异常标准时适用。
items.generated.rules.1.text: 如果柱形编码月度泄放量，那么相对于显示月份，May 属于低泄放情况；在没有已声明严重阈值或异常政策时，图表本身不能确立是否应采用标准跟进而非升级处理。
items.generated.rules.1.component: 柱到月份及竖轴水量编码；缺失的严重程度阈值
items.generated.rules.1.conditions: 在分流要求超出相对比较的明确阈值或政策时适用。
items.generated.rules.2.text: 只有当 May 不是需要主动分流的低泄放情况时，后台归档才是适当的；如果图表编码泄放量，明显最低的 May 柱就不支持该条件。
items.generated.rules.2.component: 柱到月份及竖轴水量编码；归档资格关系
items.generated.rules.2.conditions: 如果归档排除需要跟进的低泄放情况，则适用。

Review the monthly reservoir release dashboard and decide whether May should be handled as a standard low-release case or escalated as a critical low-release anomaly for this reporting cycle.
Escalate May to critical low-release anomaly review
The chart shows May at roughly 8,500 m3, dramatically below every other displayed month (about 17,500–40,000 m3), supporting critical anomaly escalation. No explicit threshold is shown.

If the bars encode monthly reservoir release volume on the common vertical axis, and the reporting workflow treats a month visibly far below all other displayed months as a critical low-release anomaly, then that month should be escalated. This severity convention is assumed because no explicit routing threshold is printed.
bar-to-month and vertical-axis volume encoding; anomaly-to-critical-routing relation
Applies to the displayed months and only if relative extremity is an accepted critical-anomaly criterion.

If the bars encode monthly release volume, May is a low-release case relative to the displayed months; absent a stated critical threshold or anomaly policy, the chart alone does not establish whether standard follow-up rather than escalation is required.
bar-to-month and vertical-axis volume encoding; missing severity threshold
Applies when routing requires an explicit threshold or policy beyond relative comparison.
Background filing is appropriate only when May is not a low-release case requiring active routing; a visibly minimal May bar would not support that condition if the chart encodes release volume.
bar-to-month and vertical-axis volume encoding; filing eligibility relation
Applies if filing excludes low-release cases needing follow-up.

Review the monthly solar generation dashboard and decide whether May should be handled as a standard low-output case or escalated as a critical low-output anomaly for this reporting cycle.
Escalate May to critical low-output anomaly review

The chart shows May at roughly 8,500 MWh, dramatically below every other month (about 17,500–40,000 MWh), indicating a critical low-output anomaly. No explicit numerical escalation threshold is provided.

If the vertical axis labeled "Solar output (MWh)" encodes bar height on a common increasing scale and each month label identifies its aligned bar, then May's much shorter bar represents substantially lower output than the other displayed months. If this degree of relative isolation is treated by the routing workflow as a critical anomaly, May should be escalated.
bar-height-to-solar-output encoding and relative-anomaly-to-critical-routing relation
Applies only if all bars use the same y-scale and the workflow permits critical escalation based on an exceptionally low relative monthly value; no explicit escalation threshold is displayed.

If the same bar encoding applies, May is a low-output month. If critical routing requires a stated numerical threshold or other documented anomaly criterion that is not provided, the chart alone cannot establish critical severity; under a policy of routing unthresholded low-output cases to ordinary follow-up, May should receive standard follow-up.

Applies only if critical escalation requires an explicit criterion and standard follow-up is the default for visibly low output without that criterion.

Escalate May to critical low-pumping anomaly review
May is roughly 8,500 m3, dramatically below every other displayed month (about 17,500–40,000 m3), indicating a critical low-pumping outlier. No explicit severity threshold is shown.

If the vertical axis labeled "Pumping volume (m3)" encodes pumping volume with higher bar tops representing greater volume, and the routing practice treats an isolated month that is visibly far lower than every other displayed month as a critical low-pumping anomaly, then that month should be escalated.
bar-height-to-pumping-volume encoding and assumed anomaly-to-critical-routing relation
Applies to the displayed monthly bars; critical-routing convention is an assumption because no explicit severity threshold or routing policy is supplied.

If the chart establishes that May is low-pumping but no supplied policy defines a critical threshold, and the workflow defaults unthresholded low-pumping cases to standard follow-up rather than escalation, then May should receive standard follow-up.

Requires a default-to-standard policy assumption; no such policy is visibly stated or supplied.

rules.text: If the dashboard title is an intended descriptor of the overall 2018-2023 capacity trend, and the routing task maps an increasing overall capacity trend to expansion follow-up, select the expansion-follow-up route.
rules.component: dashboard title interpretation and task-to-route relation
rules.conditions: Applies only if the title is authoritative for the requested overall trend rather than merely descriptive; the task provides no explicit routing policy table.

rules.text: If the vertical axis encodes Capacity Index with larger values higher on the page, and overall trend is assessed by comparing the first and last plotted years, a final mark lower than the initial mark indicates a decline; if decline maps to the decline-response route, select that route.
rules.component: vertical-axis encoding, endpoint trend comparison, and task-to-route relation
rules.conditions: Applies if the plotted endpoints, rather than the chart title or intermediate peak, define the overall trend; the decline-to-route mapping is inferred from the option wording.

rules.text: If the vertical axis encodes Capacity Index with larger values higher on the page, and the latest multi-year segment is treated as approximately stable despite small movement, the routine-monitoring route may fit a stable recent trend.
rules.component: vertical-axis encoding, recent-segment interpretation, and task-to-route relation
rules.conditions: Applies only if routing is based on recent stability rather than the full 2018-2023 period; no explicit stability threshold is supplied.

At 2010, the chart shows Hydroelectricity at a higher generation share than Nuclear energy (blue series is about 32% versus red about 26%).

The blue circular series is Hydroelectricity and is read against the left blue y-axis; the red dashed square series is Nuclear energy and is read against the right red y-axis. A higher generation-share comparison requires decodable, comparable 2010 values from those axes or another explicit common-scale statement; screen-space height alone is not comparable across separate y-axes.
series-to-axis binding and cross-axis comparability
Applies to the displayed dual-axis chart. No common numeric y-scale or 2010 value inscription is visible.

If one source is established to have the higher 2010 generation share, the task directs routing that source to the higher-share follow-up workflow; if no source is established as higher, an archive outcome would require a stated unresolved-comparison fallback.
task-to-routing relation
The public task requests the source with the higher 2010 generation share. No archive fallback policy is supplied.

proposal.brief_basis: The chart’s highest plotted per-barrel value is at 1980 (about $38), exceeding 1976 and 1986.

rules.text: If the x-axis year labels bind each blue marker to its year, and the vertical tick scale is the plotted per-barrel price scale described by the chart title/task, then larger printed vertical-axis values represent higher per-barrel costs. proposal.brief_basis: The yearly trend’s highest plotted mortality count is in 2018 (slightly above the 2017 level and higher than 2010); the y-axis is visually inverted, with larger counts lower on the chart.

rules.text: If the x-axis year labels bind each plotted marker to its reporting year, the y-axis labeled Count encodes mortality count, and larger Count values are positioned lower because the printed y ticks increase downward, then the lowest plotted marker represents the annual mortality peak. If the x-axis year labels bind each plotted marker to its reporting year, the y-axis labeled Count encodes mortality count, and larger Count values are positioned lower because the printed y ticks increase downward, then the lowest plotted marker represents the annual mortality peak. For this task, route that peak year to its matching escalation option.

action.option: Route the surveillance record to rising-case escalation follow-up

proposal.brief_basis: The chart’s reported case counts rise sharply across the displayed period, from near zero to roughly 1,500 cases (despite the inverted visual y-axis orientation).

rules.text: If the horizontal labels encode the displayed reporting sequence from left to right, the vertical axis labeled "Count" uses its printed tick values, and larger printed values are lower on the page, then the line's movement from near the 0 tick at the left toward below the 1400 tick at the right encodes an increase in reported cases. For this task, an increasing reported-case trajectory maps to rising-case escalation follow-up.
rules.component: time-series axis direction, count-scale decoding, and task routing relation
rules.conditions: Applies to the plotted blue case-count series and assumes the printed Count ticks, rather than conventional upward chart geometry, define the metric direction.

rules.text: If chart geometry is interpreted by the usual upward-is-higher convention despite the printed Count tick ordering, the line's downward screen movement would appear to represent a declining trajectory; under the task labels, a declining trajectory maps to declining-case stabilization review.
rules.component: alternative visual-direction interpretation and routing relation
rules.conditions: Only applies if the printed vertical tick labels are disregarded or treated as nonauthoritative.

rules.text: If routing requires an explicit policy threshold or sustained-trend criterion beyond the general instruction to select the pathway that best matches the observed trajectory, the chart alone does not provide that threshold; background monitoring could be retained pending such a criterion.
rules.component: possible missing operational threshold
rules.conditions: Applies only if an unstated escalation policy threshold is required; no such threshold is supplied in the task materials.

observations.content: The title reads "Month vs. Number of cases," and the vertical axis is labeled "Count."
Printed y-axis ticks show 0 near the top, then 200, 400, 600, 800, 1000, 1200, and 1400 at progressively lower positions.
The leftmost blue marker is positioned close to the 0 tick, while the rightmost blue marker is below the 1400 tick.

observations.location: horizontal axis and blue plotted series
observations.content: The blue line runs from left to right across the dated horizontal labels and its markers generally move lower on the page.

chains.option_label: Route the surveillance record to rising-case escalation follow-up
chains.claim: Using the printed inverted vertical scale, the plotted case-count series rises across the displayed period, ending above 1400 cases versus near zero at the start; this supports rising-case escalation follow-up.

observations.content: The blue line and markers generally move lower on the page from left to right.

chains.option_label: Route the surveillance record to declining-case stabilization review
chains.claim: If conventional screen geometry were used instead of the printed y-axis ordering, the downward line could be read as declining; this conflicts with the labeled-scale interpretation.

Displayed data show a steady increase from about 132k visits in 2017 to 171k in 2020. The chart does not display 2013-2016, so full-window sustained-growth status cannot be verified; recent-upswing monitoring best fits visible evidence.

If the task requires an end-to-end 2013-2020 determination but the chart displays only 2017-2020, sustained growth over the full window cannot be verified; under that limitation, the recent-upward-shift monitoring option is the non-overclaiming fit.

action.option: Route to sustained growth planning for an enrollment pattern that indicates broad multi-year expansion

proposal.brief_basis: The displayed trajectory rises consistently from about 260 enrolled patients in 2017 to about 374 in 2020, indicating multi-year expansion; the chart visibly shows 2017-2020 despite the stated 2013-2020 review scope.

rules.text: If the chart title and axes bind the teal line to telehealth follow-up enrollment by year, and higher vertical position represents more enrolled patients on the labeled y-axis, then successive higher points at later year ticks indicate enrollment growth over the displayed years. This supports sustained-growth planning only if the displayed years adequately establish the requested full review-window pattern.

rules.text: If the visible series covers only a recent subset of the requested review window and rises within that subset, then the task's route for an upswing that still warrants observation may be appropriate rather than treating the subset as proof of broad full-window expansion.

Route to sustained growth planning for an enrollment pattern that indicates broad multi-year expansion

The displayed trajectory rises consistently from about 260 enrolled patients in 2017 to about 374 in 2020, indicating multi-year expansion; the chart visibly shows 2017-2020 despite the stated 2013-2020 review scope.

If the chart title and axes bind the teal line to telehealth follow-up enrollment by year, and higher vertical position represents more enrolled patients on the labeled y-axis, then successive higher points at later year ticks indicate enrollment growth over the displayed years. This supports sustained-growth planning only if the displayed years adequately establish the requested full review-window pattern.
line-series, year-axis, and enrolled-patients-axis encoding; task classification for broad multi-year expansion
Applies to the visible 2017-2020 series. The task requests a 2013-2020 assessment, but no 2013-2016 marks are displayed, so broad expansion across the entire stated window is unverified.

If the visible series covers only a recent subset of the requested review window and rises within that subset, then the task's route for an upswing that still warrants observation may be appropriate rather than treating the subset as proof of broad full-window expansion.

Applies because the x-axis visibly begins at 2017 while the task context states a 2013-2020 review scope; it does not establish the unshown earlier trajectory.

The displayed 2017-2020 enrollment series indicates growth across four consecutive shown years, which supports the proposed sustained-growth route; however, the chart does not show 2013-2016, so broad expansion across the requested full 2013-2020 review window remains an evidence gap.

action.option: Escalate this selected-region pattern for broader population review before advancing an enterprise-wide claim

proposal.brief_basis: The selected high-burden regions show a clear positive PM2.5–ER visit pattern (roughly 29/62 to 69/160), but this selected-region dashboard comparison alone is insufficient for an enterprise-wide claim.

rules.text: If the horizontal axis encodes PM2.5 exposure and the vertical axis encodes asthma ER visits on common ordered scales, the upward-right arrangement of the labeled regional points supports a descriptive positive association within the displayed regions. Because the chart explicitly limits itself to selected high-burden regions, that association does not by itself establish an enterprise-wide population pattern or claim; for the enterprise evidence-routing task, such selected-region evidence should be escalated for broader population review before advancing an enterprise-wide claim.

rules.text: If the selected high-burden regions are known outside this chart to be representative of the enterprise population and the displayed exposure–ER-visit relationship is sufficient for the intended enterprise claim, the same upward-right point arrangement could support advancing that claim.
rules.component: scope/representativeness assumption and task-to-route relation

rules.text: If the chart is treated solely as a contextual dashboard summary and no action is warranted from a selected-region comparison without additional supporting evidence, it can be retained as background reference.

action.option: Route the emergency department visit record to utilization-growth follow-up

proposal.brief_basis: Despite the chart title, visits rise overall from roughly 1,300 in 2012 to roughly 3,200 in 2023, with substantial increases after 2017; growth follow-up best fits the review-period pattern.

rules.text: If the plotted line encodes emergency department visits by year, with higher vertical position corresponding to larger values as indicated by the ascending y-axis tick labels, then a later endpoint plotted higher than the earlier endpoint indicates overall utilization growth; under the task's overall-pattern routing instruction, this supports utilization-growth follow-up.
rules.component: line-series, year-axis, y-axis, and task-to-routing relation
rules.conditions: Applies if the single red line is the reviewed Region Z utilization series and endpoint comparison is an appropriate measure of the review-period overall pattern.

rules.text: If the dashboard title is an authoritative summary of the utilization pattern, then its literal characterization of visits as declining from 2012 to 2023 supports utilization-decrease follow-up.
rules.component: dashboard-title summary to routing relation
rules.conditions: Applies only if title text overrides or resolves any apparent conflict with the plotted series.

rules.text: If routing requires a stated threshold, sustained-direction criterion, or policy rule not supplied in the task, and the plotted series has both rises and declines, then standard trend monitoring may be appropriate rather than an escalation pathway.
rules.component: task-policy requirement and mixed-series interpretation
rules.conditions: This is conditional because no routing thresholds or escalation policy rules are provided.

The horizontal axis is visibly labeled "Year" and has printed yearly ticks from 2012 through 2023.

红线在2014至2015、2018至2019以及2022至2023的绘制位置之间向下倾斜。

items.verification_invalid_raw.checks.0.reason: 绘制的下降段是直接可见的几何特征，但把缺少政策表归于chart_1的观察并不是图表观察；它涉及所提供的任务。任务未陈述该规则的前提，即必须有阈值、持续方向标准或其他政策。因此，逐年运动方向混合且缺少阈值，不足以确立常规监测是最匹配的路径。

items.verification_invalid_raw.checks.1.reason: 标题转录是获得支持的字面文字。然而，图表未明确说明标题的权威性高于绘制序列，也未说明标题措辞与图形冲突时如何解决。因此，仅凭标题不能确立本任务中通向下降路径的推导。

proposal.brief_basis: The chart values rise overall from about 850 requests in 2012 to about 2,700 in 2023, despite a small decline from the 2022 peak; the overall demand pattern is growth.

rules.text: If the x-axis years order the plotted line chronologically and the y-axis labels encode telehealth follow-up request magnitude increasing upward, then a substantially higher final plotted point than initial plotted point indicates overall growth across the displayed period; if the routing labels correspond to that overall pattern, select growth-response follow-up.

proposal.brief_basis: The hazard risk index legend marks light yellow as high; ME is light yellow, while OK and TX are dark burgundy (low).

rules.text: The map’s state fill colors encode the Hazard H risk index according to the adjacent vertical legend: pale yellow at the top corresponds to the printed High/100 end and dark burgundy at the bottom corresponds to the printed Low/0 end. If the priority hazard review list is intended to select the highest risk-index state among the offered options, select the option for the highest encoded state.

rules.conditions: Applies if the state labels identify their filled map areas, the legend governs those fills, and priority review means choosing the highest Hazard H risk index among ME, OK, and TX.

rules.text: The chart establishes relative Hazard H risk-index encoding but does not itself state the program rule, threshold, or other criterion for adding a state to priority review. Without that task-to-action criterion, a selection cannot be established from the chart alone.
rules.component: scope of chart evidence versus priority-review selection policy
rules.conditions: Applies if no external or supplied policy defines how the risk index determines priority-review inclusion.

proposal.brief_basis: The chart legend shows lighter yellow as higher incidence; Texas is light yellow near the high end, while Washington is dark low and Colorado is gray/no displayed incidence.

rules.text: If the map's vertical legend encodes incidence from burgundy at the printed low end (0) to pale yellow at the printed high end (100), then a state filled pale yellow has higher displayed incidence than a state filled burgundy. For the stated workflow, select the option for the highest-incidence jurisdiction only where all candidate jurisdictions are comparably encoded; an unlegendized gray fill cannot be ranked without an additional missing-data rule.
rules.component: legend color-to-incidence encoding; state-label-to-fill binding; highest-incidence routing relation
rules.conditions: Applies to the labeled contiguous-state map and assumes the legend governs the colored fills. It does not assign an incidence meaning to gray.

rules.text: If gray-filled jurisdictions are excluded from the displayed-incidence comparison because gray denotes unavailable or non-displayed data, then the highest displayed incidence among the remaining candidate states should be routed.
rules.component: gray-fill treatment; task-to-routing relation
rules.conditions: This is an additional assumption: the chart provides no printed gray legend entry or explanation.

The region in Colorado's map position is gray and has no visible state abbreviation label.

rules.text: For this choropleth, a state's fill color encodes incidence according to the vertical legend: the pale-yellow end adjacent to the printed 100 and “High” is higher than the dark-burgundy end adjacent to the printed 0 and “Low.” If the gray Alabama-area polygon denotes unmapped/no incidence value rather than a value on that scale, it is not eligible to exceed a mapped state; among the offered eligible state records, route the highest-incidence one.

rules.conditions: Applies only if the legend governs the state fills and gray is an unmapped/missing category. The chart does not visibly print an Alabama label or define gray.

observations.content: The title visibly reads “Incidence of Condition A in US States.”

The inscription “UT” is placed inside a dark-burgundy state polygon.
A gray state polygon is visible in the position where the Alabama option would refer, but that polygon has no visible “AL” inscription and gray is not shown on the legend.

proposal.brief_basis: The May 06 Station X (blue) segment is minimal—near the chart baseline and far below the other stations' demand—supporting low-demand routing. No explicit routing thresholds are shown.

rules.text: If the legend binds blue to Station X and the stacked bar encodes visitor counts cumulatively from zero, then the top of the blue segment at May 06 represents Station X's visitor count; if the routing program classifies that count as low, low-demand response is appropriate.
rules.component: legend-to-series binding, stacked-bar value decoding, and assumed demand-to-routing threshold
rules.conditions: Assumes the clipped lower axis does not alter the cumulative stack meaning and that the low-demand threshold includes the May 06 Station X value; no threshold is supplied.

rules.text: If a stacked bar is clipped by a y-axis beginning at 1,500, the visible height of a bottom segment measures only the portion above 1,500, not its full magnitude; without supplied routing thresholds, a conservative default may be normal monitoring.
rules.component: truncated-axis interpretation and assumed default task relation
rules.conditions: Applies because the chart has no visible routing criteria and the supplied task has no policy table or interpretation rule establishing a low-demand cutoff.

observations.content: A blue swatch is visibly labeled "Station X".
A thin blue section is visible at the bottom of the May 06 stacked bar, ending only slightly above the horizontal axis line.
The lowest visible labeled y-axis tick is "1,500".
The green and orange sections above the blue section are visibly much taller than the visible blue section.

chains.option_label: Route May 06 to low-demand response

observations.content: The horizontal axis line aligns with the printed "1,500" tick, and the May 06 blue section meets that lower chart boundary.

The map legend shows lighter yellow as higher risk; Illinois is the lightest/highest-risk state among the listed options, while Kansas is dark low-risk and Delaware is midrange.

action.option: Open Delaware (DE) risk detail for routine monitoring

proposal.brief_basis: The legend shows higher risk toward light yellow and low risk toward dark red; DE's orange index is higher than NM's dark-red low index, while RI is gray/unscored. The available DE option's workflow label conflicts with the requested priority wording.

rules.text: If a state's fill color is encoded by the displayed vertical Risk Index legend, the pale-yellow end at the printed "High"/"100" end represents higher risk than the dark-red end at the printed "Low"/"0" end; fills not represented by the gradient, such as gray, have no stated risk-index value.
rules.component: map fill-color-to-risk-index encoding
rules.conditions: Applies only where the state fill is intended to use the displayed gradient; gray is not assigned a meaning by the visible legend.

rules.text: If routing is restricted to the offered state-record options and gray/unmapped states are not eligible for a risk comparison, the offered state with the highest legend-decoded risk is the available choice most consistent with the stated highest-risk routing criterion.
rules.component: task relation between eligible offered records and highest-risk routing
rules.conditions: Requires that selection is limited to the listed options and that unscored or unmapped states are excluded; it does not establish that the selected offered state is highest among all states shown.

rules.text: If the routing criterion literally requires the highest-risk state across the entire dashboard rather than only among offered eligible records, an offered record can be selected only if the chart establishes that it exceeds every other mapped state.
rules.component: scope of dashboard-wide highest-risk criterion
rules.conditions: Applies when "highest risk state in the dashboard" is not restricted to the available options.

The legend shows higher risk toward light yellow and low risk toward dark red; DE's orange index is higher than NM's dark-red low index, while RI is gray/unscored. The available DE option's workflow label conflicts with the requested priority wording.

If a state's fill color is encoded by the displayed vertical Risk Index legend, the pale-yellow end at the printed "High"/"100" end represents higher risk than the dark-red end at the printed "Low"/"0" end; fills not represented by the gradient, such as gray, have no stated risk-index value.
map fill-color-to-risk-index encoding
Applies only where the state fill is intended to use the displayed gradient; gray is not assigned a meaning by the visible legend.

If routing is restricted to the offered state-record options and gray/unmapped states are not eligible for a risk comparison, the offered state with the highest legend-decoded risk is the available choice most consistent with the stated highest-risk routing criterion.
task relation between eligible offered records and highest-risk routing
Requires that selection is limited to the listed options and that unscored or unmapped states are excluded; it does not establish that the selected offered state is highest among all states shown.

If the routing criterion literally requires the highest-risk state across the entire dashboard rather than only among offered eligible records, an offered record can be selected only if the chart establishes that it exceeds every other mapped state.
scope of dashboard-wide highest-risk criterion
Applies when "highest risk state in the dashboard" is not restricted to the available options.

proposal.brief_basis: Chart shows Service Design at 51%, the highest feedback share among categories.

rules.text: If the chart title identifies the displayed measure as public-service feedback share and each percent inscription is attached to its category's marker, the category with the largest printed percentage is the highest-share feedback category; the task routes that category to priority follow-up.
rules.component: title/percent-label encoding and highest-share routing criterion
rules.conditions: Assumes the percent inscriptions, rather than the vertically plotted marker positions on the generic 'Value' axis, encode feedback share.

rules.text: If the vertical marker position on the 'Value' axis is the intended encoding of feedback share, a marker higher on that common axis represents a larger share; the task routes the highest such category to priority follow-up.
rules.component: vertical position/axis encoding and highest-share routing criterion
rules.conditions: This conflicts with treating the printed percentages as the share values; the axis is labeled only 'Value,' so this interpretation is uncertain.

Route Service Design to public feedback priority follow-up
Chart shows Service Design at 51%, the highest feedback share among categories.

If the chart title identifies the displayed measure as public-service feedback share and each percent inscription is attached to its category's marker, the category with the largest printed percentage is the highest-share feedback category; the task routes that category to priority follow-up.
title/percent-label encoding and highest-share routing criterion
Assumes the percent inscriptions, rather than the vertically plotted marker positions on the generic 'Value' axis, encode feedback share.

If the vertical marker position on the 'Value' axis is the intended encoding of feedback share, a marker higher on that common axis represents a larger share; the task routes the highest such category to priority follow-up.
vertical position/axis encoding and highest-share routing criterion
This conflicts with treating the printed percentages as the share values; the axis is labeled only 'Value,' so this interpretation is uncertain.

action.option: Route to tourism growth planning

proposal.brief_basis: The plotted new-tourist line rises from about 1,100 in 1880 to about 3,000 in 1891, despite the chart title saying “Decreasing.” The visible data trend supports growth planning.

rules.text: If the single plotted line is the dashboard's New tourists series, the horizontal axis encodes chronological year left-to-right, and higher vertical position maps to a larger number of new tourists using the upward-increasing y-axis, then a line ending higher than it begins indicates growth over the reviewed period. If the routing labels are intended to map a growth trend to growth planning, select the growth-planning route.
rules.component: line-series, axes, and trend-to-route relation
rules.conditions: Assumes the plotted line, rather than the title text, is the authoritative encoding of Town Z new-tourist values and that a net increase warrants growth planning; no explicit routing policy is supplied.

rules.text: If the chart title is an authoritative statement of the tourism trend and the word "Decreasing" is intended as the routing-relevant classification, then the decline-response route is appropriate.

rules.text: If contradictory chart signals cannot be resolved because neither an authority hierarchy nor a routing threshold is supplied, then the trend cannot be classified reliably for escalation and routine monitoring is the conservative route.

Review the Town Z new-tourist trend dashboard for 1880-1891, then choose the follow-up route for the tourism operations trend.
Route to tourism growth planning
The plotted new-tourist line rises from about 1,100 in 1880 to about 3,000 in 1891, despite the chart title saying “Decreasing.” The visible data trend supports growth planning.

If the single plotted line is the dashboard's New tourists series, the horizontal axis encodes chronological year left-to-right, and higher vertical position maps to a larger number of new tourists using the upward-increasing y-axis, then a line ending higher than it begins indicates growth over the reviewed period. If the routing labels are intended to map a growth trend to growth planning, select the growth-planning route.
line-series, axes, and trend-to-route relation

Assumes the plotted line, rather than the title text, is the authoritative encoding of Town Z new-tourist values and that a net increase warrants growth planning; no explicit routing policy is supplied.
If the chart title is an authoritative statement of the tourism trend and the word "Decreasing" is intended as the routing-relevant classification, then the decline-response route is appropriate.
title-to-trend and trend-to-route relation
Assumes the literal title overrides the contradictory plotted-line geometry; the chart supplies no rule resolving this conflict.

If contradictory chart signals cannot be resolved because neither an authority hierarchy nor a routing threshold is supplied, then the trend cannot be classified reliably for escalation and routine monitoring is the conservative route.
conflict-resolution and task-to-route relation
Assumes routine monitoring is the appropriate default for unresolved evidence; this default is not stated in the task.

The blue line begins at the vertical alignment of the printed x-axis tick "1880".

axes
The horizontal axis is visibly labeled "Year"; the vertical axis is visibly labeled "Number of New Tourists" and has printed values increasing upward from "0" to "4,000".
Route to tourism growth planning
Under the plotted-line encoding, Town Z's new-tourist series increased from 1880 to 1891; therefore growth planning is the proposed route.
chart title

Keep on routine tourism monitoring
The chart gives conflicting visible trend signals and no supplied rule states which signal governs; under a conservative unresolved-evidence default, keep the trend on routine monitoring.

Route to tourism growth planning
Despite the chart title saying “Decreasing,” the plotted new-tourist series rises overall from about 1,100 in 1880 to about 3,200 in 1891, with strong late-period growth.

If the blue line is the series encoded by the chart axes, the horizontal axis orders years left-to-right and higher vertical positions correspond to larger values on the upward-labeled tourist-count scale, then a higher endpoint at the later year indicates an increase over the review period. If an increasing new-tourist trend is to be routed to growth planning, select the growth-planning option.

Assumes the plotted line, rather than the title wording, is the authoritative record; assumes the unlabeled blue line represents the y-axis measure and that increasing trends map to growth planning. The task supplies no explicit routing policy.

If the chart title is the authoritative characterization of the tourism trend and its word "Decreasing" is intended as the routing signal, then the trend should be treated as declining. If a declining new-tourist trend is to be routed to decline response, select the decline-response option.
title-as-authoritative trend characterization; trend-to-route relation
Applies only if literal title wording overrides the plotted line and if declining trends map to decline response; neither precedence nor routing policy is explicitly supplied.

If conflicting title and plotted-line signals, together with the absence of an explicit routing threshold or precedence rule, prevent a reliable trend classification, then retain routine monitoring rather than infer a growth or decline route.
ambiguity handling and task-to-action relation
Requires a conservative default of routine monitoring under unresolved evidence conflict; this default is not stated in the task.

Review the Town Z new-tourist trend dashboard for 1880-1891, then choose the follow-up route for the tourism operations trend.
Route to tourism growth planning
The chart rises overall from about 1,000 new tourists in 1880 to about 2,650 in 1891 despite a late dip; the title says “Decreasing,” but the plotted series visibly shows net growth.

If the blue line is the new-tourist series, the horizontal year ticks bind its endpoints to 1880 and 1891, and higher vertical position maps to a larger number of tourists, then the relative endpoint positions indicate net change across the review period. If routing is based on net growth, a positive net change maps to growth planning.
line-series/axis encoding and net-trend-to-route relation
Assumes the plotted line, rather than the title, is authoritative for the new-tourist measure and that the task uses whole-period endpoint change; no explicit routing policy is supplied.

If the chart title is an authoritative textual classification of the tourism trend, then its word "Decreasing" indicates a decline classification. Without a supplied rule resolving conflict between that classification and the plotted line, routine monitoring is a conservative route.
title-as-authoritative trend classification and conflict-to-route relation
Assumes the title is intended as a valid trend label and that unresolved contradictory chart evidence should not trigger a directional response.
plot at x-axis ticks 1880 and 1891
The blue line begins at the 1880 tick aligned with the y-axis tick labeled "1,000" and ends at the 1891 tick above the y-axis tick labeled "2,500".
axes
The horizontal axis is inscribed "Year" and has ticks from 1880 through 1891; the vertical axis is inscribed "Number of Tourists" with increasing labeled ticks upward.

Under the endpoint-change interpretation, the plotted new-tourist series shows net growth from 1880 to 1891 despite the final downward segment, supporting growth planning. The route mapping is an evidence gap because no explicit policy table supplies it.

action.option: Route to tourism growth planning

proposal.brief_basis: Despite the chart title saying “Decreasing,” the plotted new-tourist series rises overall from about 950 in 1880 to about 2,940 in 1891, supporting growth planning; there is only a late dip after the 1890 peak.

rules.text: If the horizontal axis labeled "Year" orders the plotted line from 1880 to 1891 and the vertical axis labeled "Number of Tourists" uses the visible numeric ticks with larger values higher on the page, then a line endpoint higher at 1891 than at 1880 indicates a higher new-tourist count at the end than at the start. If routing is based on overall endpoint growth, that interpretation supports growth planning.

rules.conditions: Assumes the single blue line represents Town Z new tourists for the labeled years and that endpoint change, rather than the title or only the latest year-to-year movement, is the routing criterion.

rules.text: If conflicting chart signals or the absence of a supplied routing threshold prevents a reliable growth-versus-decline classification, then the conservative available route is routine monitoring.

Review the Town Z new-tourist trend dashboard for 1880-1891, then choose the follow-up route for the tourism operations trend.
Route to tourism growth planning

Despite the chart title saying “Decreasing,” the plotted new-tourist series rises overall from about 950 in 1880 to about 2,940 in 1891, supporting growth planning; there is only a late dip after the 1890 peak.

If the horizontal axis labeled "Year" orders the plotted line from 1880 to 1891 and the vertical axis labeled "Number of Tourists" uses the visible numeric ticks with larger values higher on the page, then a line endpoint higher at 1891 than at 1880 indicates a higher new-tourist count at the end than at the start. If routing is based on overall endpoint growth, that interpretation supports growth planning.
line-series encoding, axis bindings, endpoint comparison, and growth-route relation
Assumes the single blue line represents Town Z new tourists for the labeled years and that endpoint change, rather than the title or only the latest year-to-year movement, is the routing criterion.
If the chart title is the authoritative trend classification for the routing task, then the literal word "Decreasing" in that title supports the decline-response route.
title-to-routing classification relation
Applies only if the title is intended to override or summarize the plotted series for the decision.
If conflicting chart signals or the absence of a supplied routing threshold prevents a reliable growth-versus-decline classification, then the conservative available route is routine monitoring.
uncertainty-to-monitoring relation
Assumes routine monitoring is the designated fallback when no explicit routing policy resolves conflicting evidence.
plot and axes
The blue line begins at the 1880 tick near the 1,000 y-axis tick and ends at the 1891 tick below the 3,000 tick but visibly higher on the page than its 1880 endpoint.
axis labels

Route to tourism growth planning

Under the plotted-series endpoint interpretation, new-tourist count is higher in 1891 than in 1880, so the proposed growth-planning route is supported. No supplied policy explicitly states that endpoint growth mandates this route.
title at top of chart

If the title is authoritative despite the plotted geometry, its literal classification supports decline response.
title and plotted line
The title includes the word "Decreasing," while the line's 1891 endpoint is visibly higher on the page than its 1880 endpoint.
Keep on routine tourism monitoring
The title and endpoint geometry conflict, and the supplied task contains no routing threshold or tie-break rule; under a conservative fallback convention, routine monitoring is supportable.

Review the City A population dashboard for 2010-2015, then choose the follow-up route for the population planning workflow.
Route to population growth planning
The plotted population rises from about 2,000 in 2010 to 3,000 in 2015, despite the chart title calling it shrinking; the visible line supports growth planning.

If the blue line is the dashboard's total-population series, the horizontal axis maps left-to-right positions to the printed years, and the vertical axis increases upward as labeled, then a line endpoint aligned with a higher y-axis tick at the later year represents population growth; if the routing workflow maps observed growth to growth planning, select the growth-planning route.

action.option: Open 2012 Canada indicator follow-up record

proposal.brief_basis: The dashboard chart shows Canada’s red 2012 point above the United States’ blue 2012 point, indicating a larger 2012 value.

rules.text: If the red dashed-square series is Canada and the blue solid-circle series is United States, and both use one shared vertical scale that increases upward, then a higher 2012 mark represents a larger 2012 indicator value.
rules.component: series-to-country binding and shared increasing vertical-position encoding
rules.conditions: Assumes the colored side labels bind to their same-colored series and that the chart uses a comparable shared y-scale; no labeled y-axis values are visible.

rules.text: If the printed numbers beside the colored marks are their countries' indicator values, then the 2011 and 2013 annotations show that screen height does not reliably rank the countries' numeric values; consequently, without a printed 2012 value or explicit shared-scale information, the 2012 comparison cannot be established from mark height alone.
rules.component: annotation-to-value binding and cross-series scale comparability
rules.conditions: Applies only if the nearby printed numerals are values for the respective marks; it identifies an evidence gap rather than supplying a 2012 value.

action.option: Open 2012 0-19 years demographic planning follow-up record

proposal.brief_basis: In the chart at 2012, the blue 0-19 years point is visibly higher than the red 20-39 years point, indicating the larger population.

rules.text: If the blue circular series is the 0-19 years series and the red square series is the 20-39 years series, and both series use the same vertically comparable population scale, then the series mark higher on the page at the same year encodes the larger population. Under the task instruction, open the follow-up record for that larger cohort.

rules.conditions: Applies to the 2012 marks only; requires that the two colored axes/series are on a common or directly comparable population scale.

rules.text: If the differently colored left and right axes can use independent, unshown, or non-comparable scales, then screen-space height of the blue and red 2012 marks alone does not establish which cohort has the larger population. Open 2012 0-19 years demographic planning follow-up record
In the chart at 2012, the blue 0-19 years point is visibly higher than the red 20-39 years point, indicating the larger population.

If the blue circular series is the 0-19 years series and the red square series is the 20-39 years series, and both series use the same vertically comparable population scale, then the series mark higher on the page at the same year encodes the larger population. Under the task instruction, open the follow-up record for that larger cohort.
series-to-cohort binding, vertically encoded population comparison, and routing criterion
Applies to the 2012 marks only; requires that the two colored axes/series are on a common or directly comparable population scale.

If the differently colored left and right axes can use independent, unshown, or non-comparable scales, then screen-space height of the blue and red 2012 marks alone does not establish which cohort has the larger population. Without another public dashboard value or scale bridge, the comparison is unresolved; routine archive is the available non-cohort routing option.
